newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-ARGENTINE COURT BANS CHILAVERT FOR 13 MONTHS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINE COURT BANS CHILAVERT FOR 13 MONTHS.

text.p: An Argentine appeals court on Friday confirmed a 13-month professional playing ban on Paraguay captain Jose Luis Chilavert for punching a stadium assistant during a match in April 1994.
It is the first time a player has been sentenced under a law designed to clamp down on soccer hooliganism.

The court also confirmed a three-month suspended sentence on Chilavert handed down by a judge last September for the incident in an Argentine league match between his club Velez Sarsfield and Gimnasia y Esgrima de la Plata.
But legal sources quoted by the state-controlled Telam news agency said Chilavert can still appeal to the Supreme Court, and can go on playing until there is a final ruling.
Television replays at the time appeared to show the tall, heavily-built goalkeeper breaking away from a brawl with opposing players to hit the stadium assistant.
Chilavert was also convicted of attacking Gimnasia defender Sergio Dopazo after the match, which Velez lost 3-2 in the city of La Plata.
Chilavert, a Paraguayan national hero and considered one of the world's top goalkeepers, said when he was first sentenced last year that he would play elsewhere if the Argentine ban was confirmed.

He said the sentence showed he was being persecuted for being Paraguayan, and hinted it might have something to do with a goal he had scored from a free kick against Argentina in a World Cup qualifier a few days earlier.
The 31-year old Chilavert specialises in free kicks, and despite being goalkeeper has scored more times this season than any of his Velez team mates.
In late April, FIFA suspended Chilavert for four months for fighting with Colombia striker Faustino Asprilla during another World Cup qualifier the month before.
FIFA has also said it would investigate the 1994 incident.
A menacing figure in goal who wears a bulldog design on his chest, Chuilavert says he wants to become President of Paraguay one day and impose his own brand of law and order.
